newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Muscovite seeks to sue Yeltsin for nepotism.
newsitem.headline: Muscovite seeks to sue Yeltsin for nepotism.

text.p: A 25-year-old Moscow lawyer is trying to sue President Boris Yeltsin for illegal nepotism over his appointment of his daughter as an official adviser, a spokeswoman for Russia's Supreme Court said on Wednesday.
"We received the suit yesterday," the spokeswoman said, referring to a case brought by Yuri Samsonov, who works for a private firm of Moscow lawyers.
"It is being considered by a judge now. It doesn't mean it has been accepted. The decision will probably be made tomorrow," she said by telephone.
The Kremlin announced on Monday that Tatyana Dyachenko, 37, had formally been appointed an adviser to Yeltsin.
It is a role she has played unofficially for more than a year. But Yeltsin's parliamentary foes lost little time in condemning the appointment, saying it contradicted the civil service code.
The Kremlin responded to their allegations of illegal nepotism by saying the code did not apply to the president and a few other top state officials.
